intro: You are standing at Cyzicus, an ancient city in Balıkesir province, whose story begins in the 7th century BC. This was a great Marmara city on the Kapıdağ peninsula, and it is remembered above all for its Hadrian temple.
history: Cyzicus was founded as a colony of Miletus. Its electrum coins became a standard of Aegean and Black Sea trade, and in antiquity its Temple of Hadrian was called the eighth wonder.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Temple of Hadrian, the Amphitheatre, the Aqueducts and the Harbour remains.
facts: Did you know? The city was once an island. A sandbar tied it to the mainland, and today it sits on the neck of the Kapıdağ peninsula. Its amphitheatre is one of only a handful of true amphitheatres in Anatolia. The Temple of Hadrian was called the eighth wonder of the world, and travellers in the fifteenth century still counted thirty columns standing. And Cyzicene electrum staters served for centuries as a common currency across Aegean and Black Sea trade.
outro: This brings our tour of Cyzicus to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
